correctness.rationale: Published group identifications reduce injective tuple orbits to labeled finite tree types. Reversible leaf insertion proves the rooted and unrooted double-factorial counts; compatible leaf orders are exactly independent left/right choices at n-1 internal vertices; equality patterns give the Stirling transforms. Direct finite generation verifies all stated sequences and fiber sizes.

The Applegate--Cameron n-tuple paper was checked and does not discuss these tree groups.

originality.rationale: No covering statement was found for the exact M3<M4<M6 injective tuple tower, the uniform factors 2^(n-1) and 2n-3, and the resulting full-tuple Stirling profiles. The component tree counts are explicitly treated as prior art.
residual_risks: Older oligomorphic-permutation-group literature may contain the individual C- or D-relation tuple profile under tree terminology.
Because the formulas follow quickly from classical tree models, an unindexed folklore statement is plausible.
The integrated hypergraph-chain statement may be mathematically new as a synthesis even if every individual sequence has appeared elsewhere.
source_inspections: Assari--Hosseinzadeh--Macpherson, Set-homogeneous hypergraphs: Sections 2.1, 3.1, 4.2, 4.3 and Remark 6.3.
Bodirsky--Jonsson--Van Pham, The Complexity of Phylogeny Constraint Satisfaction: finite rooted binary leaf structures and homogeneous C-relation.
Almazaydeh--Macpherson, Jordan permutation groups and limits of D-relations: finite D-sets as leaves of finite unrooted trees.
Applegate--Cameron, Orbits on n-tuples: general tuple-orbit growth, with no covering C/D-tree formula found in the checked text.

value.rationale: The theorem quantifies, in every arity, the orbit information lost along a natural strict reduct chain of three distinguished set-homogeneous hypergraphs and supplies exact arbitrary-tuple profiles.
